correctness.rationale: Exact conditional Bernoulli variance and Gaussian bivariate sign-angle identity produce the finite-n series; fractional Brownian scale invariance is exact. A mean-value estimate uniformly excludes the smooth covariance correction to the leading local |s-t|^{2H} term, proving a_j asymptotic and the polynomial/log/convergent regimes. Differentiating the sharp constant proves unique optimizer. Boundary assumptions and unproved extensions are explicit; finite checker supplements rather than proves the universal result.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Abramowicz–Seleznjev arXiv:1104.4920 already proves a general panel-disagreement MSE identity and optimal density under its regularity hypotheses, so these are not asserted independently novel. However its q.m. continuity/Hölder condition is violated by the fBM sign indicator at zero, and it contains neither the exact scale-invariant a_j formula nor the logarithmic-critical and slow-power regimes. None of the other stated primary theorems includes the randomization variance conditional on a single realized path, the panel sequence a_j, or the minimization of c_(H,gamma)/(2gamma-H-1). The Abramowicz–Seleznjev optimal-density formula is prior art and formally predicts the optimal power exponent after substituting local sign-angle regularity; the substantive new statement is the **exact critical/subcritical phase boundary plus its valid proof despite endpoint q.m. discontinuity**. Known Gaussian angle laws and elementary power sums are ingredients of the proof, not the complete claimed classification. An unlocated general theorem may still imply it, so priority is qualified.

value.rationale: Unlike quadratic-mean-continuous random fields covered by earlier stratified Monte Carlo theorems, the fractional Brownian sign integrand does not even possess a quadratic-mean limit at its time-zero endpoint. This singularity causes a genuine power/log/rate-loss phase transition in independent random quadrature, and a sharp nonuniform grid improves the full mean-square constant for every H in (0,1). This informs discretization design for sign/occupation observables and is not an arbitrary finite invariant or merely a routine numerical computation. No global optimality over unrelated schemes is claimed.
